newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran's Sirri oil reserves revised up - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Sirri oil reserves revised up - MEES.

text.p: Recoverable crude reserves at the Total SA -led Sirri oil development offshore Iran could be larger than originally thought, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"Favourable data obtained from a recently concluded 3D seismic survey at the two fields is understood to have allowed operators to boost estimated recoverable reserve figures for both structures by as much as 50 percent," MEES reported.
The Sirri E field was initially thought to hold recoverable reserves of 436 million barrels, and Sirri A 50 million barrels.
"It appears that further upward revisions could be forthcoming by the end of the field development stage," the Cyprus-based weekly reported.
Total signed a ground-breaking $600 million deal with state-owned National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) last year to develop the Sirri E and Sirri A oil and gas fields.
The French firm secured the deal after U.S. President Bill Clinton issued an executive order banning a proposed deal on Sirri between NIOC and Dupont Co unit Conoco Inc.
Total has said that production from the Sirri fields will begin in early 1998, rising to 120,000 barrels per day (bpd).
It began drilling operations in June.
"This plateau production rate may be revised upward in the light of recent developments on the reserve front," MEES said.
Malaysian state oil firm Peroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) has a 30 percent stake in the Sirri project.
